page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The five criteria
lines: Whittaker used the following criteria for
steps.why: Each criterion separates kingdoms at a different level: cell structure splits prokaryotes from eukaryotes; body organisation and nutrition separate protists, fungi, plants and animals; reproduction and phylogeny confirm the groups.
common_mistakes: Writing habitat as a criterion. Habitat is not one of Whittaker's criteria.
Listing only two or three criteria — the full list of five carries the two marks.
steps.memory_tip: Count five: cell structure, body organisation, nutrition, reproduction, phylogeny.
steps.margin_note: A numbered list of all five criteria is the complete answer.

steps.label: Recap

lines.text: Five criteria decide the five kingdoms.

steps.why: A one-line recap fixes the count: five criteria, five kingdoms — quick to recall in the exam hall.
common_mistakes: Writing the five kingdom names instead of the five criteria — the question asks for the criteria.
steps.memory_tip: Five criteria for five kingdoms — the two fives pair up.
steps.margin_note: Optional recap line; the marks are in the list above.

insider_note: All five criteria named earns full marks; three criteria typically earns one of the two.
